title: How to Photograph Products When Your Inventory Ships from China (You Never See It)
description: Dropshipping from China means you never handle inventory. Here's how to still create unique, converting product photos.

blocks.text: Dropshippers face a unique photo problem: they never touch their inventory. Products ship direct from supplier to customer. So how do you get unique, high-quality photos when you can't shoot the actual product?
Here's the workflow that actually works.
The Supplier Photo Problem
Most dropshippers use supplier photos directly. This means:

items.text: Google algorithm treats you as duplicate content

blocks.text: Fixing this is the difference between profitable dropshipping and burning ad spend.
Option 1: Order a Sample
The gold standard. Order one unit of each product you plan to sell. Shoot it yourself.
Cost: $10-50 per SKU. Payback: Massive.
For every sample you receive:

items.text: Build a full listing photo suite

blocks.text: Option 2: Aggressively Rebuild Supplier Photos
Can't order every SKU? Rebuild:

items.text: Download the highest-resolution supplier photos available

blocks.text: Result: Photos that no longer match the supplier's originals in reverse-image search. Not perfect, but a massive improvement.
Option 3: Composite Multiple Supplier Photos
Take:
Export a transparent PNG from edit-photo, then place it into the final scene or layout with a general design editor. Keep the original and transparent master so the composition remains reversible.
Use Rights-Safe Source Images

If a source image contains a watermark, obtain an unwatermarked file from the rights holder or create your own photo. edit-photo does not remove watermarks, and removing ownership marks without permission can create legal and marketplace risks.
Never—ever—upload a watermarked photo to your store. It kills trust faster than anything else.
The Consistency Rebuild
Supplier photos come in wildly different styles from different manufacturers. Your store looks like a chaos of vendors.

Suddenly your store looks like one cohesive brand instead of an Alibaba scraper.

The Reality Check
You will never fully match a brand that shoots its own products. But you can get 80% of the way there through disciplined editing.
The gap between "supplier photo dumpster" and "80% brand quality" is the difference between failed dropshipping and profitable dropshipping.
